definitions.explanation: The two opposite ends of something, whether physical (a rope, bridge, table) or abstract (a spectrum, range).

examples.japanese: ロープの{両端|りょうたん}を{持|も}つ。
examples.english: Hold both ends of the rope.

examples.japanese: テーブルの{両端|りょうたん}に{花|はな}を{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: I placed flowers at both ends of the table.

examples.japanese: {橋|はし}の{両端|りょうたん}に{警備員|けいびいん}が{立|た}っていた。
examples.english: Security guards were standing at both ends of the bridge.

notes:
READING:
Also read as りょうはし in casual speech, but りょうたん is the standard reading.

WORD FORMATION:
{両|りょう} (both) + {端|たん} (end, edge)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {両端|りょうたん}を{持|も}つ: to hold both ends
- {両端|りょうたん}から: from both ends
- {両端|りょうたん}に: at both ends
